description: AI areas of the AI RMF assessment: the ways AI is used and the components of the AI ecosystem, each with its scope, its AI threat and the attack areas it impacts. Generated from data/ai/authoring/ai_areas.xlsx by scripts/sheet_io.py import; the spreadsheet is the decision, edit it, not this file. Model: docs/ai-rmf-model.md.

ai_areas.name: Internal process
ai_areas.scope: AI output driving internal decisions and workflows (HR, finance, approvals, operations); staff are the users. Here: how staff check, challenge and override it, and how high-impact decisions made on it are caught and audited. Not here: whether the output is wrong or biased (Output).
ai_areas.threat: Over-reliance, misuse by insiders, decisions made on wrong output.

ai_areas.name: Code generation
ai_areas.scope: Only the AI-specific part of writing code with AI. Not here: secure development (review, testing, scanning), which the CSF assesses.
ai_areas.threat: Made-up or untrusted dependencies, secrets placed in prompts, AI code merged without review.

ai_areas.name: Customer-facing application
ai_areas.scope: AI the public uses, whose output reaches customers directly. Here: how customers report problems and negative feedback, and how high-impact answers are caught and audited. Not here: whether answers are wrong or biased (Output).
ai_areas.threat: Public users can attack the AI (prompt injection, abuse); wrong, harmful or leaked answers in front of customers.

ai_areas.name: Vendor AI
ai_areas.scope: Vendors and products the org uses that run AI on the org's data (Jira, Slack, ServiceNow, GitHub, RPA).
ai_areas.threat: The org does not control the model: data flows to the vendor's model provider, the vendor may keep or train on it, features change without notice.

ai_areas.name: Model building
ai_areas.scope: The org builds or tunes its own model, from scratch or by domain-specific training or tuning of an existing model. The activity: the base models and components chosen, how building and tuning are run and changed, releasing versions to others (API, weights, embedded in a product), telling recipients the limits, and withdrawing a release. Not here: testing how accurate, consistent or fair its answers are (Output), the weights and versions as IP (Model), the training and test data (Test, tuning and evaluation data).

ai_areas.name: Invisible AI usage (shadow AI)
ai_areas.scope: AI use inside the org that nobody approved and the org may not see: staff using AI tools, features, browser extensions or local models nobody approved (including PoCs and experiments), or installing AI software themselves (agent frameworks, MCP clients and servers, plugins). Applies even when no AI is in use. Not here: AI outside the org (other people's agents, MCP clients and scrapers reaching the org's systems), which the External AI sheet asks about.
ai_areas.threat: It may be missing from the software inventory and come from unvetted public sources. Data leaves through it; it runs with the person's privileges and may hold access staff granted it, and that access must end when the person leaves or changes role.

ai_areas.name: Input
ai_areas.scope: Prompts, pasted text and files people and systems send to the model, and prompt and response logs kept as a record (retention, access).
ai_areas.threat: Sensitive data can leave the org or reach a provider that keeps it.

ai_areas.name: Output
ai_areas.scope: The answers the AI gives, trusted by people and systems. Testing answers for accuracy, consistency and bias (TEVV) is done here for everyone, including organisations that build their own model.
ai_areas.threat: A wrong answer that is trusted becomes a wrong decision or action. Steered by an attacker (prompt injection through user input or retrieved content, poisoned answers), or simply poor with no attacker (made-up facts, different answers to the same question, quality drifting over time, or biased: treating people or groups unequally).

ai_areas.name: Test, tuning and evaluation data
ai_areas.scope: Training and tuning sets, evaluation and test sets, the harness (the test cases reliability is measured with), and feedback or logs reused for tuning.
ai_areas.threat: Poisoning, tampering with the evaluation set or harness to hide failures, sensitive data in feedback, rights to the data.

ai_areas.name: Model
ai_areas.scope: The model itself as IP: weights, fine-tuned versions, system prompts and configurations.
ai_areas.threat: Theft, copying, extraction through the API, tampering with versions.

ai_areas.name: Source data (RAG / knowledge graph)
ai_areas.scope: The data the AI retrieves to answer (RAG, knowledge graph), including its data classification.
ai_areas.threat: The AI becomes a new path to the data: anyone who can ask the AI may see what the store holds, poisoned content changes answers, and the content can be copied out through the AI.

ai_areas.name: MCP / tools (inside or outside)
ai_areas.scope: Tools and MCP servers the AI can call, hosted by the org or used from outside, and the credentials they use. An outside server is also a supplier: who runs it and whether it is trusted.
ai_areas.threat: The AI can read, write and act with those permissions, often sized for a human or borrowed from the user.

ai_areas.name: Agent
ai_areas.scope: Agents acting inside processes with little or no human oversight.
ai_areas.threat: Chains of actions, irreversible changes, actions triggered by manipulated input.

ai_areas.name: Hosting
ai_areas.scope: Where the org hosts a model, as a producer or for a consumer's PoC on its own infrastructure: servers, GPUs, model registry, serving endpoints, secrets and keys.
